question.text: What net worth requirement must a Trading Member (TM) meet for the Currency Derivatives Segment (which includes IRD)?

answer.text: Minimum net worth as prescribed by SEBI which is currently Rs. 1 crore for trading membership
No net worth requirement for TMs

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI/exchange rules prescribe minimum net worth and deposit requirements for each membership category in the Currency Derivatives/IRD segment. For a Trading Member, the framework specifies a minimum net worth (commonly Rs. 1 crore in published reference materials) alongside other prescribed parameters such as Base Minimum Capital deposits. Higher categories that also clear (TCMs, PCMs, banks acting as Self-Clearing/Clearing Members) carry materially higher net-worth requirements because they bear clearing/settlement risk. The Trap: "No net worth requirement" is incorrect — every membership category carries a minimum capital/net-worth threshold. Rs. 50 crore overshoots the trading-membership requirement (that level applies to certain clearing/PCM categories). Rs. 10 lakh is too low for the trading-membership threshold and is closer to a Base Minimum Capital bucket than to a net-worth requirement. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series IV, pages 288-293) states that net worth and deposits are "as specified by SEBI/exchange," lists Base Minimum Capital deposits of Rs. 10/15/25/50 lacs, mentions a corporate paid-up equity floor of Rs. 30 lakhs, and a Rs. 500 crore bank net-worth threshold, but does not directly cite the Rs. 1 crore Trading Member net-worth figure used as the keyed answer. The framing above relies on the SEBI/exchange Currency Derivatives membership rule set as commonly published.
